Interactive — pick an item

Console, field, or both?

Local gauges, hand valves, the flame and the plume have no transmitter — the round is the only way the plant learns about them.

Interactive — climb the heater

What stands at each height?

Legs lift the burner to 2.0 m so it is worked from below; platforms at 4.0 and 6.9 m reach the peep doors and the stack instruments — every reading has a place you must climb to.

Interactive — click a highlighted item (station 6, fuel oil train)

What a station shows

Each station lists its items with Read, Look or Operate; the label on the picture and the row in the panel are the same item.

Part 1 · summary

What part 1 settled

  • The console sees transmitters; the field sees gauges, valves, flame and smoke.
  • H-100 has three working levels: grade, 4.0 m and 6.9 m.
  • Each station shows items to read, to look at or to operate.

Part 2

How is the round walked, read and recorded?

Part 2 · the plan

A fixed route, a fixed sheet

  1. Twelve stationsthe route from the muster point
  2. Moving in the 3-D plantbuttons, labels and close-ups
  3. Reading a gaugethe scale, the needle, the resolution
  4. The rounds sheetwhen a reading counts as right
  5. Lookingflame, plume and peep door

Interactive — click a station

Twelve stations, one route

The route follows the feed, then the fuel and air, then climbs the heater — walk it in the same order every time so nothing is skipped.

Interactive — click a highlighted control (station 2)

Moving and working in the 3-D plant

Every Read, Look and Operate writes a line to the event log — the exercises are graded from that log.

Interactive — read the dial

Reading a local gauge

Read the scale divisions first, then interpolate between ticks — a reading is good to about half a division.

Interactive — when does a reading count as right?

The rounds-sheet rule

$$|r-v|\le \max(0.03\,|v|,\ d)$$
$r$your reading
$v$value the plant shows now
$d$reading resolution

Numbers pass within 3 % or one resolution step; states (open, running, clear) must match exactly — the sheet is graded against the live plant, not a fixed key.

Items you look at, not read

Flame, plume and peep door

Look atNormalNot normal
Burner flameshort, brightlong and lazy; roaring; out
Stack plumecleargrey haze; black smoke
Peep doorclosed after useleft open

Peep-door platform at 4.0 m · Illustration (Gemini) · IMG-06

Face shield down, stand to the side, and close the door: an open peep door lets tramp air in.

Part 2 · summary

What part 2 settled

  • Twelve stations in a fixed order, from the muster point to the 6.9 m platform.
  • Read, Look and Operate each write a line to the event log.
  • Read the scale before the needle; interpolate to half a division.
  • Readings pass within 3 % or one resolution step; states must match.

Part 3

What do the hand valves do, and how are they moved safely?

Part 3 · the plan

Fifteen hand valves act on the model

  1. Locks and sealsvalves the page will not move
  2. What a wrong position doesmodel runs, valve by valve
  3. Lining up before light-offevery valve where it belongs
  4. Tell, move, watch, logthe order of a field move

Valves with a lock or a seal

Some valves are not the operator's to move

ValvePositionWhy
V-109 E-100 drainLChot oil to grade
V-110 PSV-101 inletCSOclosed = no relief

The page refuses to move them, as a lock or seal would; a permit and a supervisor are needed.

A closed relief-valve inlet removes the last protection of E-100's tube side.

Interactive — model runs from design, valve moved at t = 0, no operator action

What does a wrong valve position do?

A closed block valve on the feed starves the coil and the low-flow trip acts within seconds — one hand valve can stop the unit.

Interactive — click to open or close

Line up the feed and fuel before light-off

Check every valve against the P&ID line-up before the BMS sequence starts — the BMS cannot see a hand valve.

The order of a field move

Tell, move, watch, log

Tell the console firstthey will see the plant respond
Move one valve, slowlyone change at a time can be undone
Watch the response, both sideslocal gauge and DCS trend
Log it"Hand valve V-107 OPENED in the field"

Part 3 · summary

What part 3 settled

  • Locked and sealed valves move only under a permit.
  • A closed feed or fuel block valve trips H-100 within seconds.
  • An open bypass or vent changes the plant without any alarm.
  • Tell, move, watch, log: one valve at a time.

This deck

Key Takeaways

1

Walk the same route every round, so nothing is skipped.

2

Read the scale before the needle; record states exactly.

3

Believe a line-up only after you have seen every valve.

4

Tell the console before you move a valve, and log every move.
